title: Document agent-generated provenance and engine scope limits in AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING
description: Two documentation gaps noted in code review: (1) Provenance: 5 of the 11 git commits are literal `[autonomous phaseN]` agent-generated merges, meaning large portions of the codebase were produced by an AI without human review markers. This is not disclosed anywhere, so future maintainers may over- or under-trust the code. (2) Scope overstatement: README markets the project as "done once, done right" and implies broad safety, but the engine is single-threaded, local-only, with no network/async and no streaming backpressure (it reads a whole directory of file paths into a sorted Vec and processes line-by-line). The bounded-memory/deterministic guarantees hold only for this single-process, ordered, local model. Fix: add a short, accurate "Provenance" note (agent-generated portions, review status) and a "Scope and Limits" section (single-threaded, local input only, no concurrency/backpressure, net/async out of scope, fuzzing needs nightly) to README and/or CONTRIBUTING. Preserve the existing AGENTS.md landing-the-plane workflow instructions intact.

title: Make fused and invariant-ppt Cargo features functional (currently inert)
description: Cargo.toml declares two features: fused and invariant-ppt. Their comments claim they "Enable the fused rule evaluation engine" and "Enable PPT-style runtime invariant logging". In reality src/lib.rs lines 317-328 declare `pub mod invariant_ppt;` and `pub mod fused;` UNCONDITIONALLY (no #[cfg(feature=...)]), and none of the module bodies contain cfg gating either. Therefore the features gate nothing: the modules are always compiled, and CI running `cargo test --all-features` gains zero extra coverage. This is a misleading no-op feature flag. Fix: make the features real and meaningful. Recommended approach: add `default = ["fused", "invariant-ppt"]` to [features], gate `pub mod invariant_ppt;` with #[cfg(feature = "invariant-ppt")], gate the `invariant_ppt::assert_invariant(...)` calls inside `Pipeline::process_event` with the same cfg, gate `pub mod fused;` with #[cfg(feature = "fused")], and add `required-features = ["fused"]` to the `[[example]]` entry for 17_fused_rule_engine so it does not break default builds. Result: `cargo build --no-default-features` excludes them, `cargo build --all-features` includes them, and the comments become accurate.

title: Harden PIIRedaction: field targeting and nested-value awareness
description: In src/lib.rs PIIRedaction::execute (around line 1387) redaction is implemented as: for every value in the event object, if it is a String, run `pattern.replace_all(s, "[REDACTED]")` for each pattern. Problems: (1) it blindly scans EVERY string field, including fields that are not PII (no way to target specific fields); (2) it does not traverse nested objects or arrays, so PII inside nested structures is missed; (3) it will re-redact an already-redacted value (turning "[REDACTED]" patterns back into "[REDACTED]") and can corrupt already-safe data; (4) there is no idempotency guard. Improve by: allowing optional field targeting (if a field allow-list is provided, only those fields are scanned; otherwise all string fields as today for backward compatibility), recursively traversing nested objects and arrays, and skipping values equal to the literal "[REDACTED]" token to avoid double work. Keep the existing `PIIRedaction::new(patterns)` constructor working unchanged for backward compatibility.

title: Modularize src/lib.rs (3188-line monolith) into focused modules
description: src/lib.rs is a single 3188-line file containing: Event type and helpers, the full PipelineError taxonomy (5 error kinds + codes), Metrics/LatencyStats, the Stage trait + Pipeline::process_event, InputSource (stdin/file/dir), the Parser trait + NDJSON/JSONArray/Syslog parsers, every built-in stage (FieldSelect, FieldRemap, PIIRedaction, DerivedFields, Filter, RequiredFields, TypeChecking, ValueConstraints, StdoutOutput, FileOutput, Deadletter), Config (YAML), the common_redact_validate_pipeline preset, PluginRegistry, and a large inline `mod tests`. It is difficult to navigate, review, and extend, and every stage repeats ~15 lines of Stage + marker-trait + ReplayableStage boilerplate. Split lib.rs into focused modules (e.g. event.rs, error.rs, metrics.rs, pipeline.rs, input.rs, parser.rs, stages/ (one file per stage or a stages.rs), config.rs, preset.rs, plugin.rs) and move the inline tests into module-level #[cfg(test)] mod tests blocks (or a tests/ dir). Preserve the exact public API: lib.rs should re-export everything so existing `use feedme::{Pipeline, FieldSelect, ...}` imports keep working unchanged.

title: Enforce or document the fail-closed validation guarantee
description: README states the mechanical guarantee "Validation failures cannot be silently ignored". This is only true if the user has added a Validator-stage (RequiredFields / TypeChecking / ValueConstraints) to the pipeline. A pipeline with no validator stage silently passes invalid events through. This is an opt-in guarantee presented as absolute, which is misleading. Resolution options (pick one, prefer the code option if low-risk): (A) Add a pipeline-level fail-closed toggle, e.g. `Pipeline::require_validation(true)` that returns an error at process_event time if no stage implements the Validator marker trait, OR a default final Validator that rejects events failing a configured schema; or (B) if code change is too invasive, precisely document in README and lib.rs docs that the guarantee is conditioned on the presence of a Validator stage. Recommended: implement option (A) as a lightweight `require_validation` flag on Pipeline (default false to preserve backward compatibility) plus document it. Keep public API additions additive.

title: Wire cargo-fuzz into CI and document the nightly requirement
description: The fuzz/ directory is a separate cargo-fuzz workspace (fuzz/Cargo.toml uses libfuzzer-sys 0.4 and cargo-fuzz metadata). It is excluded from the main workspace (root Cargo.toml has `exclude = ["fuzz"]`) and requires a nightly toolchain plus `cargo fuzz`. It is not exercised by CI (.github/workflows/test-and-coverage.yml only runs cargo test/clippy/fmt/tarpaulin/audit/publish). As a result the fuzz targets can silently break and the project advertises fuzzing without ever running it. Fix: (1) add a CI job (separate matrix entry using `nightly` toolchain) that installs cargo-fuzz and runs `cargo +nightly fuzz build` (or a short `cargo +nightly fuzz run <target> -- -runs=1000`) for the fuzz targets; and (2) document the nightly + cargo-fuzz requirement clearly in README and CONTRIBUTING so contributors know how to run fuzzing locally. Ensure the main stable test suite and release flow are unaffected by the nightly job (allow it to be non-blocking or clearly marked).
